problem.standards: From 30 September 2026 the local offer must cover accommodation and homelessness prevention for care leavers under 25, financial support, and what every department provides.
problem.evidence: The guidance expects the offer to be co-produced and reviewed at least every two years. We start from your current offer.

outcomes: See the offer from their side
Describe what it takes a care leaver to find and use support in your offer, and where they give up.
Recognise when care leavers are consulted on decisions already made, and what that does to trust.
Explain what the law and the September 2026 guidance require, separating entitlements from discretionary support.
Use Lundy's model to plan how care leavers are recruited, paid, supported and kept safe.
Audit your offer, then rewrite sections with care leavers and test them on a phone.
Plan a review at least every two years that tells care leavers what changed, overseen by the corporate parenting board.

pillars.title: Lundy's model of participation
pillars.stance: Write the offer with the people it is for
pillars.stance_line: Hearing care leavers takes four things. Most consultations stop after the first two.
items: A safe place to give views, at a time that works, with care leavers paid for their time.
Support to form and share their views on the offer.
The people who make the decisions in the room, and listening.
Care leavers see what changed because they spoke up, and what didn't and why.
pillars.base: Laura Lundy's model of participation (2007), with Roger Hart's ladder of participation (1992) and Sweller's cognitive load theory (1988).

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils nationally on participation and co-production, including Middlesbrough, where the leaving care offer was revised and relaunched with young people, and Buckinghamshire, where young people named and shaped a new participation service.
He founded the Care Leavers National Movement, and brings care leavers and decision makers into the same room.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
